newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Local and offshore appetite for South African bonds drove the market firmer on Friday after government's key R150 bond broke key technical resistance at 15 percent in after-hour trade on Thursday.
"There are still lots of buyers out there but sentiment is bit nervous because the market has moved a long way over the last few days," a senior bond trader commented.
The R150 stock started the week around 15.31 percent and had moved to a best intraday level of 14.905 percent at 1613 GMT from 14.975 percent late on Thursday.
The week was characterised by healthy buying from across-the-board which traders attributed to a strong U.S. T-bond, improved money market conditions and a stable rand.
Expectations that money supply and private credit extension numbers would slowly start turning better were also behind the upbeat sentiment.
Next week, direction was seen from March consumer inflation, money supply, private sector credit extension data and trade data, starting with the CPI figures on Wednesday.
Money supply and credit extension data are scheduled for release on Friday and trade is due in the second half of the week.
Bond traders expected more strength early next week
"The trend is definitely still down but there could be some caution because the market has come a long way," one said.
Foreigners were net sellers of 37.61 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 155.42 on Wednesday, the Bond Exchnage said.
Nominal cumulative volumes were 35.11 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 5.31 billion rand on Wednesday.

It was a sluggish day on the forex market with the rand holding a tight range. Trade was marked by small amounts of importer dollar demand which was matched by dollar supply by local mining houses, forex traders said.
At 1413 GMT the rand was at 4.4505/4535 on a range-bound U.S. unit from 4.4535/4565 late on Thursday.
"It was dead quiet today. Importer demand around the 4.4550 level was met by local mining house supply but we are talking small amounts," according to a trader at a big local bank.
He expected the currency to maintain its established 4.44 to 4.47 range next week.
"We're looking at a very stable trend...it's a pure demand/supply situation at the moment," the trader added.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.2759/3062 yen from 28.2152/2410 yen, 0.3853/3857 marks from 0.3868/3873 marks and 7.2600/2671 rand against sterling from 7.2593/2686 rand.
On the money market, leading banks all quoted their three-month NCDs rates lower at between 16.45 to 16.50 percent offered from 16.55 percent previously.
South Africa's money market shortage fell to 7.504 billion rand on Thursday from 7.853 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
